Core thesis risk (urea glut) is easing, not fully cleared (9M profit still down YoY), so this is an upgrade to HOLD, not to ADD. DOWNGRADED this run (dedicated fundamentals deep-dive, Oct 13): beyond the already-known FY26 profit decline (PAT -12.3% YoY, EPS Rs 3.43 vs Rs 3.90), a deeper health check found deterioration across four separate axes over several years -- ROE fell to 7.28% from 15.1% (FY24), ROIC to 8.84% from 23.2% (FY22), current ratio to 1.25 from 1.86 (FY22), and D/E rose to 0.29 from 0.20 (FY22). ROE/ROIC are now BELOW the 11.5% risk-free rate -- the earning power no longer clears the bar a quality holding should. Despite this, CPHL trades at the richest P/E of the three pharma holdings (18.5x vs SEARL 11.3x, GLAXO 9.5x) -- the market isn't pricing the deterioration in. One down year with a weakening balance sheet, priced at a premium multiple, is enough to trim -- not yet the multi-quarter break that would justify a full EXIT.
